question: What is the main psychological feature of illness anxiety disorder (hypochondriasis)?

options.A: Complete lack of awareness regarding bodily changes
options.B: Intentional simulation of physical disease for attention
options.C: Frequent hallucinations involving internal organ failure
options.D: Excessive anxiety about having a serious illness

explanation: You've got this! The core thing to remember here is constant, overwhelming worry about having a severe medical condition, even when medical tests show everything is fine. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h1)

question: How do patients with illness anxiety disorder usually react to normal, everyday body sensations like a slight muscle twitch?

options.A: They report them exclusively to family members only
options.B: They ignore them completely as routine physiology
options.C: They misinterpret them as signs of catastrophic disease
options.D: They use them to plan healthy physical exercise routines

explanation: Think of it this way: a normal minor ache gets blown completely out of proportion, making the patient convinced it's a hidden, dangerous sickness. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h1)

question: To officially diagnose illness anxiety disorder, how long must the symptoms of worry last?
explanation: Memory tip for clinicals: psychiatric diagnoses like this one usually require a persistent timeframe of at least six months before it's made official. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which behavior is very common for a patient dealing with illness anxiety?

options.A: Consistently ignoring all physical pain without worry
options.B: Repeatedly checking the body for lumps or abnormalities
options.C: Voluntarily stopping all interactions with healthcare workers
options.D: Seeking immediate surgery for nonexistent conditions

explanation: You will often see patients engage in compulsive checking—like constantly scanning their skin, checking their pulse, or probing for swollen lymph nodes. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h2)

question: How can experiencing a severe illness during childhood affect a person later in life?

options.A: It ensures the individual becomes a proficient medical doctor
options.B: It completely eliminates any fear of normal aging processes
options.C: It can create a lasting hypersensitivity to bodily vulnerabilities
options.D: It guarantees immunity against developing anxiety disorders

explanation: Early life bumps and health scares can teach a child that the human body is super fragile, planting the seeds for health anxiety down the road. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is a common spark or trigger that sets off an acute episode of illness anxiety?

options.C: Major life stressor or personal loss
options.D: Consuming too much dietary sodium daily

explanation: When life throws a major stressor or emotional pain our way, dormant health worries can flare up into full clinical anxiety. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is the key difference between care-seeking and care-avoiding illness anxiety behaviors?

options.A: Care-avoiding patients demand unnecessary surgery, while care-seeking patients take herbal remedies
options.B: Care-avoiding patients rely on nurses, while care-seeking patients refuse all nursing interventions
options.C: Care-seeking patients visit doctors frequently, while care-avoiding patients stay away from medical facilities
options.D: Care-seeking patients never feel anxious, whereas care-avoiding patients have panic attacks daily

explanation: It is all in the name: care-seekers run to the hospital for reassurance, while care-avoidors run away from anything medical out of fear of getting bad news. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h4)

question: What usually happens shortly after a care-seeking patient gets normal test results from a doctor?

options.A: The anxiety returns and doubt creeps back in
options.B: The patient is permanently cured of all health fears
options.C: The patient stops visiting hospitals for the rest of life
options.D: The patient develops severe physical paralysis

explanation: Medical reassurance rarely lasts long for them. Soon enough, doubt creeps back in, and they start questioning if the lab results were a mistake. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why can it be extra challenging to build trust with patients who have illness anxiety?

options.A: They are physically incapable of speaking with medical staff
options.B: They often feel dismissed or ridiculed by providers in the past
options.C: They refuse to answer any questions about their family history
options.D: They only communicate through written letters and notes

explanation: Since past clinicians may have brushed them off with 'there is nothing wrong with you,' these patients expect nurses to disbelieve their real emotional pain. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which mental health condition often shows up right alongside illness anxiety disorder?
explanation: Keep this clinical pearl in mind: depression and general anxiety very commonly walk hand-in-hand with severe health-related worries. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h5)

question: A patient keeps asking you to check their blood pressure and look at a tiny skin mark. What is the best first nursing action?

options.A: Acknowledge the patient's anxiety, then gently redirect the conversation to a non-health topic
options.B: Tell the patient firmly that their behavior is foolish and they need to stop worrying
options.C: Immediately call the physician to order blood tests and a dermatology consult
options.D: Perform a thorough physical examination of the skin spot to completely reassure them

explanation: Spot on! Validating their feelings without feeding into the endless reassurance cycle helps break the habit of obsessive body-checking. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why is setting specific check-in times helpful when caring for a patient with illness anxiety?

options.A: It forces the patient to stay confined to their bed all day
options.B: It guarantees that a physician will discover a hidden disease
options.C: It eliminates the need for any psychiatric medications
options.D: It reduces the constant, disruptive demands for continuous reassurance

explanation: Having a structured schedule shows the patient they are supported without letting endless health fixation take over the whole shift. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is widely considered the best standard psychological therapy for illness anxiety disorder?
explanation: CBT is the gold standard! It helps patients catch those scary thought patterns about their health and reframe them in a healthier way. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why are Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs) sometimes prescribed for severe hypochondriasis?

options.A: To lower the overall intensity of obsessive health worries and treat depression
options.B: To cure any undiagnosed viral infections hiding in the bloodstream
options.C: To cause mild sedation so the patient sleeps through doctor appointments
options.D: To physically block pain receptors in the muscles and internal organs

explanation: SSRIs help balance the brain chemicals tied to anxiety and obsession, making it much easier for the patient to participate in therapy. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h7)

question: How can untreated illness anxiety disorder negatively affect a patient's finances?

options.A: Through repeated unnecessary medical consultations and diagnostic tests
options.B: By forcing the patient to buy expensive athletic equipment daily
options.C: Through heavy fines imposed by public health departments
options.D: By requiring mandatory long-term stays in luxury hospitals

explanation: Constant 'doctor shopping' and endless medical scans add up fast, leading to massive medical bills and financial stress over time. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common complication of chronic hypochondriasis?

options.A: Financial stress from excessive medical appointments
options.B: Risks from unnecessary invasive medical procedures
options.C: Strain on marital and family relationships
options.D: Permanent physical immunity to all infectious diseases

explanation: You got it! Illness anxiety definitely doesn't give you superpower immunity; instead, it brings relationship strain, money troubles, and risks from needless procedures. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h8)
